title: A Autopsy for the Confession
premise: Estate lawyer Yara Zhou is called to probate the will of Edmund Vale, a reclusive tycoon whose death was ruled an accident — but the will names a beneficiary who, by every record, died thirty years ago. When a second body surfaces dressed in clothes stolen from Yara's own closet, she realizes someone is framing her inside a decades-old cover-up she's accidentally reopened. Following forged identities, a burned orphanage, and Vale's guilty confessions hidden in plain sight, Yara uncovers that the 'dead' beneficiary is alive, has been killing to keep his stolen identity, and has been watching Yara because she is the daughter he never knew he had. In the end, she chooses the law over blood, luring him into confessing on record before he can make her his final erasure.
about_author: Oscar Reyes is a former probate clerk who spent a decade handling the estates of the unclaimed and the unidentified, an experience that haunts every page he writes. He lives in a coastal city he refuses to name, and 'A Autopsy for the Confession' is his third novel.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Yara Zhou, POV. Yara is summoned to read the will of Edmund Vale and finds a beneficiary listed as 'Milo Ferro' — a boy whose death certificate is older than the will itself. Her instinct for irregularities, honed by three 'accidents' she quietly solved, pricks awake. Emotional beat: the thrill of an impossible document, shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with a cold open from the victim's final hours. A stranger is found dead in Yara's own stolen coat and scarf, in her neighborhood, holding a photocopy of Vale's will. The detective on the case is the same one whose 'accident' rulings Yara once dismantled. Emotional beat: violation — the crime has entered her skin.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She digs into the night Milo Ferro supposedly drowned: a fire at the St. Brendan's orphanage, five witnesses, and alibis so perfectly aligned they feel rehearsed. Vale's lawyer refuses to comment; one witness has just stopped answering her calls. Emotional beat: the slow horror of a lie built to last a lifetime.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Vanished
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, interspersed with a 1994 letter. Yara tracks Sister Agnes, the last living witness, to a convalescent home, arriving hours after her room was searched. Agnes leaves Yara a key and a warning: 'He signs his name with other people's hands.' Emotional beat: desperate urgency — the past is killing its witnesses in the present tense.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ashes
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The key opens a storage unit: orphanage records, Vale's private payments to five families, and a photograph of a boy with Yara's own unusual hazel eyes. Her mother, it turns out, once worked at St. Brendan's. Emotional beat: vertigo — the investigation has turned inward, and belonging becomes a question, not an answer.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A second witness dies in a fall ruled accidental, and the detective, now believing her, shares his file: someone has been pruning the past for months — since the day Yara filed Vale's probate. She realizes her reading of the will was the trigger. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve; she started this clock.

chapters.title: Confession in Duplicate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In Vale's sealed personal effects she finds two wills — one public, one private, in which Vale confesses he helped a boy fake his death to escape an abusive uncle, then watched 'Milo' become a parasite wearing a dead child's name. The private will names Milo as the sole heir of everything, including his crimes. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy of a dead man's honesty.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mirror File
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following the photograph and hospital birth records, Yara confirms the impossible: Milo Ferro survived the fire, stole his own death, and is the man who has been watching her — because her mother was his sweetheart, and Yara may be his daughter. He leaves her a note: 'You look like her.' Emotional beat: identity shattered; the hunter learns he has been courting her.

chapters.title: A Autopsy for the Confession
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, the climax. Yara stages a reading of Vale's private will at the burned ruin of St. Brendan's, wearing a wire, betting that Milo cannot resist hearing himself legally named and acknowledged. He comes, confesses the murders as a form of inheritance — erasing everyone who remembers who he was — and moves to make Yara the last erasure. The detective's team closes in as Milo realizes the will reading was the trap. Emotional beat: terror and clarity fused.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, weeks later. Milo awaits trial, refusing to deny anything; Yara files the final probate, dissolving Vale's estate into a trust for orphanage survivors — including the families Milo's lies hollowed out. She keeps the photograph but declines his lawyer's letters. Emotional beat: bittersweet settlement — she has chosen law over blood, and belonging over identity, closing the estate and opening her own life.
